title: And touch him for a guinea
html_source: Ask to borrow some money. The guinea was a british coin originally worth about a pound sterling, or 20 shillings, but which was generally worth a lot more. By the time Ulysses was published, the coin had been replaced by the Pound/Sovereign, though the term was still colloquially in use to mean 21 shillings (it’s last official fixed value), or a generic sum, a little like saying, “see if he’ll lend you a fiver.” There is, however, a certain aristocratic connotation to using the word ‘guinea’, hence the subsequent, “he thinks you’re not a gentleman.”

 Parried again. He fears the lancet of my art as I fear that of his. The cold steelpen. 

 — Cracked lookingglass of a servant! Tell that to the oxy chap downstairs
